notes: Fixed physical limits of every Earth analog, per body (T11). They do not depend on the site: no place on Earth reproduces them. Values from NASA fact sheets and peer-reviewed measurements; each entry cites its source.

Moon.consequence: Wheel traction, sinkage, the angle of repose and how far ejected regolith flies all change; Earth tests overestimate traction and underestimate dust travel.
No wind, no convective cooling, no erosion by air; equipment sheds heat only by radiation and conduction, and lubricants and seals behave differently.

Moon.earth: ~2.4 mSv per year at the surface (magnetosphere and atmosphere shield)
Moon.target: ~1.37 mSv per day at the surface (Chang'e-4 LND)
Moon.consequence: Roughly 200 times Earth's background; long stays need shielding (e.g. regolith berms), which no Earth analog can test for dose.

Moon.target: Equator ~390 K by day to ~95 K by night; permanently shadowed polar craters below 40 K
Moon.consequence: Cold traps keep volatiles such as water ice stable for billions of years; Earth's coldest places are about 140 K warmer, so ice and materials behave differently.

Moon.earth: Sun up to 90° elevation; day–night cycle of 24 h
Moon.target: Sun within ~1.5° of the horizon at the south pole; lunar day of ~29.5 Earth days
Moon.consequence: Extreme, slowly moving shadows and glare for navigation and solar power; Earth's polar sun is the closest analog but its cycle and contrast differ.

Moon.earth: Weathered, rounded grains; moisture and air bind dust
Moon.target: Sharp, glassy, electrostatically charged regolith dust
Moon.consequence: Apollo crews reported dust clogging seals, abrading visors and degrading radiators; Earth sediments are poor simulants for abrasion and adhesion.

Mars.consequence: Wheel sinkage, slope stability and the angle of repose change; rovers tested on Earth carry about 2.6 times their Mars weight.
Wind needs far higher speeds to lift sand; parachutes, heat rejection and liquid water stability are not comparable; no analog reproduces pressure outside a chamber.

Mars.earth: ~2.4 mSv per year at the surface
Mars.target: ~0.64 mSv per day at Gale crater (Curiosity RAD)
Mars.consequence: About 100 times Earth's background, from cosmic rays and solar particles; dose and its biological effects cannot be studied at an Earth analog.

Mars.target: Mean ~210 K (-63 °C) with daily swings of ~80–100 K
Mars.consequence: Thermal fatigue of materials, batteries and joints; the thin air stores little heat, so nights are colder than any desert of similar latitude.

Mars.earth: Regional dust storms lasting days (e.g. Bodélé, Taklimakan)
Mars.target: Seasonal regional storms and planet-encircling storms (e.g. Mars years 25, 28 and 34)
Mars.consequence: Global storms can block sunlight for weeks, as in 2018 when Opportunity lost power; Earth dust analogs share the seasonality, not the global scale.

Mars.earth: Perchlorate is rare, found mainly in the Atacama
Mars.target: ~0.4–0.6 wt% perchlorate in the soil at the Phoenix site
Mars.consequence: Toxic to humans and reactive with organics during analysis; only hyperarid deserts like the Atacama approach this chemistry, and only partly.
